title: CS25 second moment IS the additive energy E_2; its diagonal/off-diagonal split is the n^{1/2} energy-deficit wall made explicit and machine-checked
wall: W-Johnson/BGK (via the moment-method depth wall, CharSumMomentDeepWall.lean)
evidence: Two separable claims, graded independently with exact integer arithmetic (scripts/probes/_407_conn/C031_secondmoment_energy_identity.py and C031_diagonal_wall_identity.py). (A) THE IN-TREE IDENTITIES (PROVEN/correct, and re-verified by brute force): on RS[F_5,n=4,k=2] the Lean identity E[N^2]=sum_w closeCount(w)^2 = |C|*sum_{v in C} I(v) holds EXACTLY at every radius r=0..4 (match=True), the global normalizer sum_{all v} I(v)=V^2 holds exactly (match=True at every r), and the diagonal term is I(0)=V exactly. So sum_closeCount_sq_eq_card_mul_sum_ballInterCount_of_add_sub_closed, sum_jointCoverCount_eq_volume_sq, and the diagonal-separation in weightEnum_mds_le (A_0=1 > q^{-(n-k)}, hence d=0 must be split off) are all genuine, sorry-free, axiom-clean facts. The OBSERVATION that the CS25 ball-intersection cone has a mandatory diagonal/off-diagonal split with the same FORM as a Cauchy-Schwarz/L^2 diagonal is real and useful. (B) THE HEADLINE CLAIM (REFUTED): 'the CS25 second moment IS the additive energy E_2 of the RS code, and the diagonal I(0)=V is the n^{1/2} energy-deficit wall (E(mu_n)>=n^2 diagonal => list <= sqrt(n*E) >= n^{3/2})'. THREE exact disproofs. (1) WRONG OBJECT: the CS25 sum_{v in C} I(v) lives in F_q^n (dim n) and I(v) is a HAMMING-BALL-INTERSECTION count; the additive energy E_2(mu_n)=#{(a,b,c,d):a+b=c+d} lives in F_q (dim 1) and is an ADDITIVE-QUADRUPLE count. They are categorically distinct; the brute-force probe computes both and they are unrelated quantities (Part 1 = ball intersections of an RS code, Part 2 = additive energy of a subgroup). The verbal identification 'literally computes E_2 of the RS code' is an analogy, not an identity. (2) WRONG SIGN of the diagonal: in the actual CS25 Paley-Zygmund covered-set bound |close| >= (|C|V)^2/E[N^2] = |C|*V/(1+offdiag/V), the diagonal V is the GOOD leading term that ENABLES recovery (|close|->|C|*V as offdiag/V->0); it is NOT a list-size lower bound that BLOCKS. A list/BGK obstruction needs offdiag>>V (clustering), the opposite of a 'diagonal floor wall'. (3) NO 'n^{1/2} deficit' EXISTS in E_2(mu_n) at prize scale: across six prize-shaped primes (n=8..256, beta=4.5, q=1 mod n, proper subgroup, large prime: q=11593,262193,5931649,134218433,3037001089,68719484929) the exact E_2(mu_n)/n^2 is BOUNDED and rises only 2.625->2.99 (toward the generic ~3n^2), while E_2(mu_n)/n^3 -> 0 monotonically (0.328->0.0117). So E_2(mu_n) ~ 3n^2 (the GOOD/Sidon-like regime, B=sqrt(E_2/n) ~ sqrt(3n) ~ Ramanujan, e.g. n=256: B=27.7 vs 2sqrt(n)=32) -- the n^2 diagonal floor of E_2 is exactly what makes the AVERAGE favorable; there is no n^{3/2} list-size wall here. The genuine prize wall is the WORST-CASE per-frequency B=max_b|sum_{y in mu_n} e_p(by)| (BGK), which an L^2 second moment is provably blind to: CharSumMomentDeepWall.lean already records that the moment method (of which the CS25 second moment is exactly the r=2, weakest rung) reaches only B <~ n^{3/4+o(1)} in the prize regime because char-p moments are valid only to depth r<=r_max=2log_n p (~7), far short of the optimal r ~ log q. So the second moment cannot even reach the n^{3/4} ceiling, let alone sqrt(n).
honest_note: PARTIAL not REFUTED because the cited Lean lemmas and the diagonal-separation structural observation are all genuine and correctly machine-checked -- only the energy-identification and the 'n^{1/2} deficit wall / list >= n^{3/2}' interpretation are wrong. The connection conflates three distinct things: (i) the RS ball-intersection second moment (CS25, dim n, Hamming), (ii) the subgroup additive energy E_2(mu_n) (dim 1, additive), and (iii) the worst-case per-frequency BGK character-sum bound (the actual open prize core). (i) and (ii) are different objects; neither is (iii). The diagonal of E_2 (the n^2 Cauchy-Schwarz floor) is the FAVORABLE term, not a wall; the sqrt(n*E_2)~n^{3/2} number is the trivial scale, not a list lower bound. The probes are exact integer arithmetic: Part-1 brute force on the literal RS[5,4,2] code (full F_5^4 space, 625 words) verifies all Lean identities; Part-2/(a) exact E_2 of mu_n at six genuine prize-shaped proper-subgroup large primes. No closure of anything; this is a refutation of a misreading plus confirmation that the second moment welds back to the moment-method depth wall (CharSumMomentDeepWall.lean) = a strictly-weaker-than-sqrt(n) corner of the BGK wall. Recommend a DISPROOF_LOG one-liner: 'C031 CS25-2nd-moment != E_2(mu_n); diagonal I(0)=V is the recovery-ENABLING term not a wall; E_2(mu_n)~3n^2 (good, no n^{1/2} deficit) at prize scale; 2nd moment is the r=2 rung of the moment ladder => subsumed by CharSumMomentDeepWall n^{3/4} ceiling.'
